content:
Dating reality shows have always been an extremely popular genre, but Apple TV has never ventured into this field. Although its newly announced series "The Last Person on Earth" is positioned as a "documentary series" rather than a "reality show," it is still the streaming platform's first dating program.

"The Last Person on Earth" will be hosted by renowned couples therapist Esther Perel and is described as an "innovative experiment."

Perel is a well-known couples therapist and New York Times bestselling author who specializes in studying interpersonal relationships.

Perel is also the central figure of Apple TV's newly announced 8-episode dating documentary series "The Last Person on Earth."

According to the press release: "In the show, seemingly mismatched couples will be carefully matched by Perel and a team of matching experts and therapists, then sent to one of the most romantic and remote destinations on Earth to embark on their journey."

It does sound exactly like a reality show, just without the negative baggage that comes with the "reality" label. I'd venture to say Apple is trying to create a more "premium" tone for its dating program, hence using the "documentary series" label.

The premiere date for the series has not yet been announced, but it is expected to debut in 2027.

Apple also announced yesterday that the streaming platform will adapt a brand-new romance novel from bestselling author Rebecca Yarros into a television series. Clearly, the streaming platform is planning to expand beyond its core genres of sci-fi, comedy, and thriller series.

Apple TV costs $12.99 per month, or can be subscribed at a discount through an Apple One bundle.
